title: Thyagarajulu Gollapalli
text:
Welcome to my website!
I am Thyagi, a Research Officer and Software Engineer at the Australian National University, where I contribute to the Underworld geodynamics software ecosystem and associated tools. My work integrates computational geodynamics, geophysics, structural geology, scientific software development, and high-performance computing for Earth science applications.
I am particularly interested in megathrust earthquakes, fault representation in geodynamic models, subduction dynamics, and mantle convection, with an emphasis on numerical methods, reproducible workflows, and open-source computational modelling.

title: About
text:
Welcome! I am a Research Officer and Software Engineer at the Australian National University. My work connects computational geodynamics, geophysics, numerical modelling, high-performance computing, and open-source research software. See my CV for more details.

Short Bio
Thyagarajulu Gollapalli is a Research Officer and Software Engineer at the Australian National University. His work focuses on computational geodynamics, geophysics, numerical modelling, and open-source scientific software. He contributes to the Underworld geodynamics codebase, including core development, user-facing interfaces, testing, debugging, documentation, and training.
His research interests include finite-element methods, Stokes-flow benchmarks, subduction-zone dynamics, megathrust seismicity, geophysical data interpretation, and reproducible scientific computing. He holds a PhD in Computational Geodynamics and Geophysics from Monash University and IIT Bombay, and a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics with Earth & Environmental Science from the Indian Institute of Science.


Brief Summary of My Research
My research combines computational geodynamics, geophysics, and scientific computing to understand Earth processes through numerical modelling and data-informed interpretation.
I work on numerical models of tectonic and mantle processes, with emphasis on subduction-zone dynamics, tectonic coupling, lithospheric deformation, and long-term loading along active margins. My PhD research investigated tectonic coupling and loading along the Sunda margin through three-dimensional regional numerical modelling.
My broader geophysical background includes gravity and geoid modelling, seismic processing and imaging, GIS, and geophysical data acquisition and interpretation. This observational foundation supports model design, validation, and interpretation.
You can see more about my research on my Research page.


Open Source Software
I contribute to the Underworld geodynamics codebase as an open-source developer, with work spanning core features, user-facing interfaces, testing, debugging, documentation, and training for the geodynamics community.
Current software and benchmarking interests include:

Underworld and Underworld3 software development.
Annulus and spherical-shell finite-element benchmarks.
PETSc, MPI, and HPC workflows for reproducible geodynamics.
Boundary diagnostics, convergence studies, and benchmark verification.
Python-based scientific computing for geodynamics workflows.

You can see more of my source code and projects on GitHub: https://github.com/gthyagi


Teaching, Workshops, and Training
I have taught and supported geophysics, spatial analysis, and Earth science courses, including undergraduate geophysical interpretation and postgraduate spatial analysis and modelling.
I have also contributed to Underworld workshops and training activities at Curtin University, AuScope, and the University of Sydney, with emphasis on practical geodynamics modelling, research software workflows, and reproducibility.
